agent_vs_you: Turn 1 (captions on the clip) was right. In turn 2 the agent treated the turn-1 subtitles as editable objects: it cropped the already-captioned clip to 9:16, which cut the burned-in subtitle lines at both sides ('ant to show you t', 'your mornings l'), and then asked a generative video-edit to 'restyle the existing subtitles'. Burned-in captions are pixels; they cannot be restyled, only redone. The right move is to go back to the clean source: crop the original talk-one.mp4 to vertical around her centred face, then caption that vertical clip with a big, bold style placed above TikTok's bottom controls. Its tool, video-edit, was offered by the catalogue at the time but had no endpoint, so nothing was made (the WIRED/OFFERED filter added since then removes it). Even the right plan meets a harness limit: captions always sends the 'minimalist' template, so 'big and bold' cannot be requested today.

fix: 1) Keep the OFFERED filter (only wired tools reach the planner); it would have stopped video-edit. 2) Planner rule: captions are burned in; to restyle, resize or reframe a captioned clip, start again from the uncaptioned source (crop or trim first, caption last), never crop a captioned clip. 3) Harness: the captions call hard-codes style {template: 'minimalist'}; map the plan's style words to the subtitle API's style (a bold/TikTok-type template, or custom font size, weight, stroke and vertical position) and update captions' catalogue line from 'POORLY: big and bold is not honoured' to the supported options.
